title: Federal income tax brackets for individuals: seven rates, a 37 percent top
rule: For taxable years beginning after December 31, 2017, section 1(j) replaces the rate tables in section 1(a) to (e) with seven brackets on an individual's taxable income: 10, 12, 22, 24, 32, 35 and 37 percent. In the statute's base tables the 37 percent bracket starts above $600,000 on a joint return, $500,000 for a head of household or single filer, and $300,000 for a married person filing separately; the Treasury adjusts these amounts for inflation each year after 2018. A 2025 amendment removed the end date that limited these tables to 2018 through 2025. Section 1(h) separately caps the tax on net capital gain.
changeWatch: Any amendment to section 1(j) or 1(h), and the IRS revenue procedure each fall that sets the next year's inflation-adjusted bracket amounts; the rates themselves change only by statute.

sources.title: 26 U.S.C. 1, Tax imposed (subsection (j), Modifications for taxable years beginning after 2017, and the 2025 amendment notes)
sources.quote: Over $600,000 $161,379, plus 37% of the excess over $600,000.
